fixes.explanation: It's the opposite, friend. The teacher says, “Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place.” So he isn't holding the floor at all.
Right, baker. The teacher says, “Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place.” So at that meeting, the fool isn't the one talking.

Yes, friend. The teacher imagines someone saying they didn't know about this, and then he asks, “Does not the One who guards your life know?” He also asks whether He who weighs hearts considers it (Proverbs 24:12).

The verse doesn't go there, friend. The teacher warns the wicked man not to destroy a righteous man's resting place (Proverbs 24:15), but that's a warning. What it says about the righteous man is that though he may fall seven times, “…he still gets up…”
It's an easy guess when falling is in the picture, I'll admit. Yet the teacher says, “…he still gets up…” That's what the verse names him doing.

Yes, friend. The verse says, “but the wicked stumble in bad times.” Right before it, the teacher says a righteous man may fall seven times and still gets up. The verse puts those two pictures side by side.
I see why it's tempting, since wicked people sometimes look like they're doing great. But the teacher says, “…the wicked stumble in bad times.” Prosper isn't the word he uses.
Rest makes sense as a word, but it doesn't fit the verse. The teacher says, “…the evil man has no future…” Rest isn't the word he picks.
It's the other way around, friend. The teacher says, “For they will bring sudden destruction.” Sudden means quick, not slow.
Right, baker. The teacher says, “For they will bring sudden destruction.” Then he asks, “Who knows what ruin they can bring?” I'd rather be around people who bring cookies.
